messages.author: 330176b1955bbb3d
messages.subject: heatmap with binned values
parts:
I'm trying to show the distribution of a set of answers to 6 questions, but I'm very space constrained (and the values are sparse). I've been using a faceted histogram, but it's too big (and ugly). I'd like to try a geom_tile() heatmap, something like:

ggplot(data=testd,aes(y=question,x=year,fill=..count..)) + geom_tile()

but I can't figure out how to get the ..count.. variable, particularly binned. I've tried

# always plots bars?
ggplot(data=testd,aes(x=year,y=question,fill=..count..)) + geom_tile() + stat_bin()

ggplot(data=testd,aes(x=year,y=question,fill=..count..)) + stat_summary(fun.fill="count") + geom_tile()

etc.

testd <- data.frame(
respondent_id=rep(1:100,3),
question = c(rep("Question 1",100), rep("Question 2",100),rep("Question 3",100)),
year = runif(300,min=1976,max=2010)
)
testd$year <- floor(testd$year)

# faceted
ggplot(data=testd,aes(year)) + geom_histogram() + facet_wrap(~question,ncol=1)

Basically I'm hoping for a tile for each, say 3 years, where the color shows density/count of the number of respondents for that question that fall into that bin.

Do I need to do the binning outside ggplot2?

Thanks,
James

messages.author: 330176b1955bbb3d
messages.subject: Re: heatmap with binned values
parts:
Ah, I had not. Thanks, that's very close.

ggplot(data=testd,aes(year,question)) + stat_bin2d()

However this seems to show only 2 bins for the y axis; I've played with bins and binwidth but I don't think I'm following

# attempt to have a bin for each question (y) and each 5 years (x)
ggplot(data=testd,aes(year,question)) + stat_bin2d(binwidth=c(5,1))

This also only gives two lines on the y, almost as though it was interpreting the discrete values as (1-2],(2-3]?

ggplot(data=testd,aes(year,question)) + stat_bin2d(binwidth=c(5,.5)) gives three lines, but with a gap that I don't understand.

Ideally I'd have this just as in geom_tile with discrete values, where the tile centers on the intersection of the x and y?

Any idea of an easy way to have the label for the last bin (ie values that haven't happened yet, currently coded as 2011) be "Never Applied"? Would I need to specify all breaks in scale_x_datetime? How would that interact with changes in binning?

Thanks,
James
